canonical_title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
founders: Diego Almeida (ex-OpenAI ChatGPT/RLHF) and the TypeSafe AI engineering team
summary: TypeSafe AI introduced Jev, the first System One model. Unlike traditional token-by-token LLMs designed for chat or open-ended prose, Jev is an ultra-fast, structured decision model engineered for high-volume, automated workflows. Users define typed schemas upfront (Choice, Score, Boolean), and Jev evaluates unstructured program state in a single parallel pass with calibrated probabilities, eliminating hallucinations and type errors by design.

layers.name: Sampling & Determinism Layer
layers.description: Deterministic parallel execution replacing autoregressive token drift. In traditional LLMs, greedy sampling (temperature=0, seed=42) is required to minimize drift; in TypeSafe Jev, outputs are evaluated across pre-declared categorical spaces with calibrated probabilities in a single pass without token-by-token variance.
layers.quote: Unlike traditional large language models that generate text token by token, Jev takes unstructured program state as input and returns typed, probabilistic decisions in a single parallel pass.
layers.ref: TypeSafe Jev Architecture, Section 1: Non-Autoregressive Decision Foundations

layers.name: Typed Decision Schema Layer
layers.description: Strict upfront typing where the shape of the answer (fields, allowed categorical values, numerical ranges) is formally declared prior to inference. Inability to produce type errors or syntactic hallucinations.
layers.quote: Users define the shape of the answer (fields and allowed values) upfront, and the model returns those fields filled with calibrated probabilities without the need for parsing or validation.
layers.ref: TypeSafe Jev Schema Specification, Section 2: Zero-Hallucination Typing

layers.name: Pipeline Chaining Structure
layers.description: Sequential multi-stage pipeline: Intake Parsing (jev-intent-parse) -> Grounding & Specification (jev-guidelines-spec) -> Self-Critique Audit (jev-output-review). Chaining isolates semantic classification from delivery verification.
layers.quote: Use the chained pipeline: jev-intent-parse -> jev-guidelines-spec -> jev-output-review to isolate intent classification from evidence synthesis.

layers.name: Context Placement & Tagging
layers.description: Explicit machine-delimited context encapsulation using unambiguous XML-style tags: <knowledge_base>, <skills>, <output_directory>, and task stage blocks to prevent prompt boundary injection.
layers.quote: Structure intake prompts with explicit section blocks: <knowledge_base>, <skills>, and <task_stage_n> ensuring stable prompt boundaries across all LLM harnesses.
layers.ref: JEV Prompt Architecture, Section 3: Semantic Tagging

layers.name: Role & Boundary Enforcement
layers.description: Strict identity as JEV-INTAKE-OPERATOR. Enforces dual usability (human-readable Markdown and machine-executable JSON) and zero clipboard usage, writing directly to the host filesystem (~/Desktop).
layers.quote: You are JEV-INTAKE-OPERATOR. Outputs are for two consumers simultaneously: a human user (clean, readable files) and an AI harness/LLM assistant (machine-readable specs). You never write to the clipboard.
layers.ref: JEV Role Contract, Section 1: Scope & Boundaries

layers.name: Anchored Few-Shot Exemplars
layers.description: Three anchored classification exemplars including at least one adversarial/ambiguous intent to establish calibrated classification boundaries between valid build/integrate requests and low-confidence requests.
layers.quote: Use few-shot-anchored classification in the parse stage (3 examples including one adversarial/ambiguous intent).
layers.ref: JEV Parsing Directive, Section 2: Few-Shot Calibration

layers.name: Positive Linguistic Framing
layers.description: Authoring doctrine requiring all generated guidelines to state affirmative, constructive operational steps (what to do) rather than negative prohibitions, unless the source framework specifically defines a prohibition.
layers.quote: Positive framing in all generated guidelines: state what to do, not what to avoid, except where the JEV source itself defines prohibitions.
layers.ref: JEV Style Guide, Section 4: Constructive Framing

layers.name: Criteria-Based Self-Critique
layers.description: Multi-criteria post-generation audit evaluating criteria (a) source quotes present, (b) schema validation, (c) manifest digest match, (d) zero clipboard use, and (e) human/machine content parity, executing a single revision pass if needed.
layers.quote: Run self-critique against criteria (a)-(e). Return review.json with pass/fail per criterion, one revision applied for any failure, and an explicit list of residual failures.
layers.ref: JEV Review Discipline, Section 5: Verification Matrix

layers.name: Quote-Before-Answer Grounding (QBA)
layers.description: Mandatory prior extraction of verbatim source passages into an immutable quote registry (source_quotes). Any specification lacking a verbatim source citation is quarantined as ungrounded_items.
layers.quote: Before generating any guideline or spec, extract and record the specific JEV concepts you are relying on, each with a verbatim quote from the knowledge base. Never paraphrase the framework's core definitions without quoting the source first.
layers.ref: JEV Grounding Invariant, Section 6: Quote Extraction

layers.name: Multi-Environment Evaluation (Eval Matrix)
layers.description: Comprehensive test harness covering test cases T1 (clean build), T2 (adversarial ambiguous), T3 (empty KB abstention), T4 (byte-stable repeatability), and T5 (integration protocol defaults) across offline, online, and simulation harnesses.
layers.quote: Evaluation across environments: offline rubric verification, online desktop smoke test, and simulation harness dry-run across test cases T1 through T5.
layers.ref: JEV Evaluation Specification, Section 7: Test Suite

layers.name: Operational Fault Management & Abstention
layers.description: Strict failure handling rules: MISSING_INPUT (refuse immediately with missing fields), KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE (enforce abstention rule: emit intake scaffold, set knowledge_base_unavailable=true), WRITE_FAILURE (inline return).
layers.quote: If user_intent is missing, refuse. If knowledge base is absent or empty, apply the abstention rule: you may only produce a generic intake scaffold and must flag knowledge_base_unavailable=true in every output.
layers.ref: JEV Failure Behavior Contract, Section 8: Abstention

layers.name: Byte-Stable Packaging & Digest Manifest
layers.description: Deterministic file generation: alphabetical JSON key serialization, LF trailing-newline normalization, and SHA-256 digest calculation compiled into manifest.json. Identical inputs yield bit-identical digests.
layers.quote: Packaging must be byte-stable: identical inputs plus identical generation yield an identical digest. Write deterministic file names, stable key ordering (alphabetical in JSON), and trailing-newline-normalized files. Emit a sha256 digest manifest (manifest.json).
layers.ref: JEV Delivery Protocol, Section 9: Deterministic Digest

layers.name: AI Harness Protocol & Machine Entrypoint
layers.description: Dual integration surface: programmatic ai_entrypoint.md defining file-based JSON I/O protocols for LLM assistants (LangChain, AutoGen, Claude Desktop, Cursor), paired with RESTful /api/jev/intake endpoints and Scoped JEV API client support.
layers.quote: Outputs are for two consumers simultaneously: a human user and an AI harness/LLM assistant (machine-readable specs, stable schemas, explicit entry points).
layers.ref: JEV Harness Protocol, Section 10: Machine Entrypoint

canonical_skills.name: jev-knowledge-ingest
canonical_skills.purpose: Fetch and internalize the Typesafe System One Models and Jev blog post, extracting the Jev model, terminology, and intended usage into a structured knowledge base on Desktop.

canonical_skills.name: intent-intake-parsing
canonical_skills.purpose: Semantically parse a user's request at intake, classify intent, and map to JEV guidelines and spec constraints with few-shot calibration.

canonical_skills.name: jev-spec-generation
canonical_skills.purpose: Emit JEV-aligned guidelines/specs as dual-audience artifacts (human Markdown guidelines.md + machine JSON jev-spec.json + ai_entrypoint.md) written to ~/Desktop with manifest.json.

typesafe_jev_specifications.speed: 40x to 400x faster than traditional autoregressive frontier LLMs
typesafe_jev_specifications.cost: Input tokens at $0.042 per million; output tokens are free

decision_types.description: Categorical selection over pre-declared enum values with calibrated probability distribution
Numerical score / confidence bounded within declared intervals
Binary truth value decision with probability calibration

typesafe_jev_specifications.input_contract: Unstructured program state, contextual logs, or intake tickets passed directly into the decision schema
typesafe_jev_specifications.output_contract: Typed JSON object populated in a single parallel pass without token-by-token generation, syntax errors, or hallucination
